title: What's the dev tool or workflow trick that saved you the most time, but nobody talks about? (AI included)
author: Glass_Definition_583
selftext:
Everyone talks about the big tools (version control, engines, asset stores), but I’m more curious about those small, unglamorous things that quietly saved you hours, an odd editor shortcut, a naming convention, a debugging habit, anything that wasn't obvious until you stumbled upon it by chance.

I’m also specifically curious about AI: has any AI tool actually improved your workflow in a tangible way (code, art, audio, debugging, writing, etc.), as opposed to those that seemed cool but didn't pan out? What does your day-to-day look like with them now?



What about you?

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body: Setting proper gamestates/savestates that are reusable for testing/implementing a decent dev environment/tools for proper testing so you dont have to prompt everything you want to try out

replies.author: EQLMonk
replies.body: My literal job believe it or not lol

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Exactly why I built the game dev platform for everyone. Don't wanna say anymore or link because I advertised a bit today trying to get testers and feel like a spambot lol

comments.author: Opelmannator
comments.body: Own engine that ai can use. I havent touch any code. But iam just hobbiest.

comments.author: ipreuss
comments.body: An API that the AI can use to reproduce a game state, play the game, and poll the resulting game state. Including creating screen shots, also for automated visual tests.
